What about rto recovery time objective long service down before?
answer: RTO (Recovery Time Objective) is how long the service can be down before the business is seriously harmed: the time from failure to restored service. RPO (Recovery Point Objective) is how much data the business can afford to lose, measured in time: how far back your last good copy can be. A 4-hour RTO with a 15-minute RPO means "back up within 4 hours, losing at most the last 15 minutes of writes." How the numbers shape the architecture RPO drives your data strategy. Nightly backups give roughly a 24-hour RPO, asynchronous replication gives seconds to minutes, and synchronous replication gets close to zero.

topic: Notes: RTO vs RPO
questions: Tell me about RTO vs RPO
What does the note RTO vs RPO say?
What about near zero option cost every write waits remote?
answer: The near-zero option has a cost: every write waits on the remote copy, which adds latency, and a replica problem can block writes entirely. RTO drives your standby strategy. Backup-and-restore takes hours, a pilot light takes tens of minutes, warm standby takes minutes, and active-active is near-instant. Cost and operational complexity rise steeply at each step, which is why tiering matters. The link to SLOs is the part interviewers like. A 99.9% monthly availability SLO allows about 43 minutes of downtime. A single incident that uses a 4-hour RTO burns more than five months of error budget.

topic: Notes: Strong consistency vs eventual consistency
questions: Tell me about Strong consistency vs eventual consistency
What does the note Strong consistency vs eventual consistency say?
What about strong consistency means once write completes any later?
answer: Strong consistency means that once a write completes, any later read will immediately see that value. So, no surprises. Everyone sees the latest write right away. Eventual consistency is looser. If no new writes happen, replicas will eventually converge to the same value, but in the meantime, reads might return older data. So, strong consistency favors correctness and predictability, while eventual consistency favors availability and performance, accepting temporary inconsistency.

Tell me about SAST and DAST
answer: SAST and DAST are two complementary ways of finding security vulnerabilities in an application. SAST (Static Application Security Testing) scans the source code, bytecode or binaries without running them. It's "white-box" testing: it reads the code the way a reviewer would. DAST (Dynamic Application Security Testing) attacks the running application from the outside, like a real attacker would, with no access to the code. It's "black-box" testing.

answer: CRI is the Container Runtime Interface it defines how the kubelet talks to a container runtime like containerd or CRI-O to start and stop containers. CNI is the Container Network Interface plugins that wire up pod networking, giving each pod its own IP and connecting them across nodes. CSI is the Container Storage Interface, the equivalent for storage: how volumes get provisioned and attached to pods. topic: Notes: Forward proxy vs reverse proxy
questions: Forward proxy vs reverse proxy
Tell me about Forward proxy vs reverse proxy
answer: Key difference is which side they’re protecting. Forward Proxy sits in front of clients, it’s used when a group of users, say inside a company network, need to reach the internet, and the proxy forwards their requests out on their behalf. The outside world sees the proxy, not the individual users. Reverse Proxy, on the other hand, sits in front of servers. It protects and manages the server side, hiding the backend infrastructure from the clients making requests. So forward proxy anonymizes and controls outbound traffic for clients, reverse proxy manages and distributes inbound traffic for servers.

topic: Notes: Strong consistency vs eventual consistency
questions: Strong vs eventual consistency
Strong consistency vs eventual consistency
Tell me about Strong consistency vs eventual consistency
answer: Strong consistency means that once a write completes, any later read will immediately see that value. So, no surprises. Everyone sees the latest write right away. Eventual consistency is looser. If no new writes happen, replicas will eventually converge to the same value, but in the meantime, reads might return older data. So, strong consistency favors correctness and predictability, while eventual consistency favors availability and performance, accepting temporary inconsistency.
